rationale: Single-GPU FP32 batch=32 ResNet-18 inference, so all communication-oriented dimensions are out of scope (communication capability not_applicable per observations.json). The torch collector already ran (coverage.json: 88/88 kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences) and is not re-requested. The open uncertainty in evaluation.json is attribution: the accepted candidate (3.674 ms vs parent 4.210 ms, binding effective 'direct' with no functional replacements) self-declares three routes for call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa (captured, cuda_graph_replay, eager_fused) across only two candidate invocations, and the endpoint interpretation explicitly flags route labels as candidate-reported telemetry needing native corroboration. nsys is selected to independently prove graph replay versus eager kernel execution for that call and to give GPU-side kernel intervals and gaps inside the synchronized forward. execution_timeline is selected to associate CPU submissions with CUDA execution and locate the boundary synchronizations and per-device intervals, distinguishing GPU-busy time from host submit/sync gaps in the remaining 3.67 ms. python_runtime is rejected because it perturbs execution and host dispatch is not implicated (all kernels associated, direct binding); binding_cost is rejected because effective binding is direct with no functional replacements, leaving no binding overhead relevant to this latency objective; nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and device_telemetry are inapplicable to a single-device task with no collectives.
